claims.text: Untreated standard Inconel 718 components have typical surface conditions and baseline residual-stress profiles.
The proposed intervention is laser shock peening with high-energy laser pulses and a water overlay.
Real-time diagnostics and process control can ensure uniform shock delivery across complex component geometries.
Laser shock peening will induce a uniform, deep compressive residual-stress layer in Inconel 718.
The compressive residual-stress layer will extend several millimeters below the surface.
High-pressure shock waves generated by the laser pulses cause localized intense plastic deformation.
Laser-induced plastic deformation produces a uniform compressive residual-stress layer.
The compressive residual-stress layer mitigates crack initiation.
The compressive residual-stress layer mitigates crack propagation.
Mitigation of crack initiation and propagation improves fatigue life.
Mitigation of crack initiation and propagation improves resistance to stress-corrosion cracking.
LSP-treated Inconel 718 may have a fatigue life two to three times that of untreated Inconel 718.
LSP-treated Inconel 718 will have greater resistance to stress-corrosion cracking than untreated Inconel 718 under combined cyclic mechanical and corrosive conditions.
The treatment will remain effective under typical service conditions involving cyclic mechanical loads and corrosive environments.
Uniform treatment of highly complex component geometries depends on careful process control.
